title: Queue Smoothing and Throttling Safeguards
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines a cross-cutting standard for queue smoothing and throttling safeguards across Redwood’s public and internal services. It codifies a conservative set of behaviour guarantees, configuration templates, observability requirements, and runbook steps so that services avoid catastrophic cascading failures during load spikes while preserving predictable latency and clear cost accounting.

Motivation
----------
Incidents and SLO violations in the last 18 months have shown two recurring failure modes: (1) unbounded request queues that cause OOMs and long tail latency, and (2) aggressive drop policies that produce silent functional degradation for customers. We need a single, opinionated pattern that balances availability, fairness, and cost across the stack (edge proxies, service ingress, worker pools, and the runtime).

Scope
-----
- Applies to all Redwood public-facing services (redwood-api, routing-proxy, inference-gateway) and internal services where client-perceived latency matters (billing, telemetry-ingest).
- Includes both synchronous request entry points and async worker queues driving GPU inference.
- Does NOT prescribe model-specific batching logic or kernel-level eviction; those remain in eng-serving-runtime.

Definitions
-----------
- Admission queue: in-memory or broker queue where incoming requests wait before being served. Examples: local ring buffer in routing-proxy, Redis list for background tasks.
- Smoothing window: short time window used to convert bursty arrival to a steady feed to downstream workers (e.g., 50–200ms).
- Backpressure signal: explicit upstream indication to slow or pause senders (HTTP 429, gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED or connection-level windowing).
- Priority tier: numeric label (0=critical, 1=interactive, 2=batch) used for scheduling and admission.

Principles
----------
1. Fail predictably and loudly: prefer fast rejection (429) over indefinite queuing when backlog threatens SLOs or resource saturation.
2. Smooth short bursts locally: introduce bounded smoothing at ingress to avoid creating load spikes on GPU pools.
3. Preserve SLAs for high-priority traffic using strict caps and preemptible lower-priority work.
4. Measure end-to-end queue time and surface it as a first-class SLI.
5. Provide a single configuration overlay and a deployable template for services to inherit.

Design and Patterns
-------------------
1) Admission policy model (default):
   - Max in-flight (per instance): integer cap on concurrently processed requests. Default: 200 for small instances, 800 for inference-gpu-1.
   - Soft queue depth: per-instance queue buffer for smoothing. Default: 32 requests.
   - Hard queue depth: absolute cap after which requests are rejected. Default: 128 requests.
   - Priority partitioning: allocate queue slices per priority tier, e.g. 20% reserved for tier 0, 50% for tier 1, remainder for tier 2.

2) Smoothing component:
   - Implement a tokenized leaky-bucket that drains at a configured take_rate tuned to downstream throughput. Small smoothing windows (50–150ms) reduce transient contention and batching jitter.

3) Backpressure and retry semantics:
   - Upstream receives HTTP 429 with header Retry-After (seconds) for synchronous clients. 429 is our canonical backpressure signal across gateways.
   - gRPC clients should map RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and include Retry-After in trailers.
   - Client SDK guidance: exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts = 6, and a total retry budget per top-level request = 20s by default (shorter for low-latency paths).

4) Preemption and graceful eviction:
   - Long-running or batch requests may be preempted when higher-priority traffic arrives. Preemption is signalled with a structured error (code PREEMPTED, body includes resume token when supported).

Config templates (example YAML)
-------------------------------
This is the canonical config block used by routing-proxy and services that embed the admission controller. Services should include this block in their infra repo and allow overrides for instance class.

admission:
  enabled: true
  instance_class: inference-gpu-1
  max_in_flight: 800
  soft_queue_depth: 32
  hard_queue_depth: 128
  smoothing_window_ms: 100
  priority_slices:
    - tier: 0
      reserved_pct: 20
    - tier: 1
      reserved_pct: 50
    - tier: 2
      reserved_pct: 30
  backpressure_response:
    code: 429
    retry_after_seconds: 1

Note: defaults tuned for inference-gpu-1. Smaller instance_class should set max_in_flight <= 200 and hard_queue_depth <= 64.

Observability requirements
-------------------------
Every service implementing this standard must emit the following metrics (Prometheus style) with the specified labels:
- admission_queue_depth{instance,service,priority}: gauge (current queue depth per instance and priority).
- admission_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{le,instance,service,priority}: histogram (time spent waiting before admission).
- admission_rejects_total{reason,service,instance}: counter (reason=hard_cap|timeout|circuit_open).
- smoothing_tokens_drain_rate{service,instance}: gauge (tokens/sec).
- backpressure_signals_total{service,instance,type}: counter (type=429|grpc_resource_exhausted).

SLIs and Alerts
---------------
SLIs (measured per service, 1m and 5m windows):
- e2e_p95_latency: 95th percentile end-to-end request latency < service SLO (see service profile).
- queue_wait_p99: 99th percentile admission_queue_wait_seconds < 250ms for interactive tiers.
- reject_rate: rate(admission_rejects_total{reason=hard_cap}) < 0.1% over 5m.

Alerting rules (suggestions):
1. Alert P1 - Queue saturation: queue_wait_p99 > 500ms OR admission_queue_depth > hard_queue_depth * 0.9 for > 3m. (Pager to oncall, severity P1).
2. Alert P2 - Reject surge: increase in reject_rate by >10x baseline for 5m. (Notify slack #ops and owner team).
3. Alert P3 - Smoothing starvation: smoothing_tokens_drain_rate < configured_min for > 2m (indicates misconfiguration).

Runbook: responding to queue saturation
--------------------------------------
1) Identify scope: query metrics admission_queue_depth and admission_rejects_total; determine instances affected.
2) Short term mitigation (3–15 minutes):
   - Increase replica count of the service by +25% if autoscaling is constrained (run autoscaler override).
   - Reduce batch sizes on inference workers (if safe) to increase throughput per request.
   - If overload is caused by tier 2 (batch), temporarily set priority_slices.tier2.reserved_pct=0 and restart admission controller.
3) Medium term (15–120 minutes):
   - Route new traffic to a warmer fleet (fallback model variant or different region) via smart routing.
   - Throttle low-priority clients using rate-limiter policy by client_id.
4) Post-incident: run a traffic replay with the incident trace to tune smoothing_window_ms and soft_queue_depth.

Telemetry and tracing
--------------------
- Every admission event must add tracing spans named admission.enqueue and admission.dequeue with tags: service, instance, priority, queue_depth_at_enqueue.
- Preserve a unique request id header X-Request-Id across retries; include it in logs and metrics.

Compatibility guidelines for SDKs and clients
--------------------------------------------
- SDKs should expose: retry_budget(TimeSpan), max_attempts, and a helper for handling PREEMPTED responses.
- Client libraries must treat 429 as a signal to back off immediately; they must not automatically escalate to more retries than configured by service-level retry budget.

Testing and validation
----------------------
- Local integration test: use the admission test harness (scripts/ingress-loadtest) to validate that a service honors soft/hard caps and priority slices. The harness will: produce a mixed-priority workload, measure queue_wait_p99, and verify correct headers returned on rejects.
- Canary: when enabling changes to admission config, run a canary rollout on 5% traffic for 30 minutes and verify queue_wait_p99 and reject_rate do not regress beyond +10%.

Rollout procedure (safe path)
----------------------------
1) Add the canonical admission block to the service repo and create a feature branch.
2) Unit tests and harness tests must pass locally.
3) Deploy to staging and run the integration loadtest with mixed-priority traffic.
4) Create a canary release: route 5% production traffic to new config for 30m. Monitor SLIs.
5) If stable, progressive rollout to 25% then 100% with 30m observation windows.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Policy owner: eng-infra admission team (owner alias: eng-infra-admission@redwood.ai).
- Primary stakeholders: eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform.
- Oncall escalation: paging policy follows standard SRE rota; see eng-sre/runbooks.

Security and privacy notes
--------------------------
- Admission queues may carry tenant identifiers and prompt text. Ensure PII is not persisted to disk in unencryped form. Long-lived broker queues must be encrypted at rest and role-restricted.

Open questions and future work
-----------------------------
- Per-tenant adaptive smoothing that learns optimal smoothing_window_ms per traffic fingerprint.
- Integration with Redwood Optimize to automatically propose instance_class changes when queue_wait_p99 shows persistent growth.

Appendix: example Prometheus rules
----------------------------------
# Queue saturation alert
ALERT QueueSaturation
  IF max_over_time(admission_queue_depth[5m]) > (hard_queue_depth * 0.9)
  FOR 3m
  LABELS {severity=\"page\"}
  ANNOTATIONS {
    summary = \"Admission queue near hard cap for {{ $labels.service }}\",
    runbook = \"https://confluence.internal/redwood/eng-sre/runbooks/admission-queue-saturation\"
  }

# Reject surge alert
ALERT RejectSurge
  IF increase(admission_rejects_total{reason=\"hard_cap\"}[5m]) > (10 * avg_over_time(increase(admission_rejects_total{reason=\"hard_cap\"}[5d])))
  FOR 5m
  LABELS {severity=\"sev2\"}

Appendix: quick curl example (client guidance)
------------------------------------------------
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-Id: ${REQUEST_ID}' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium-qa","input":"Summarize quarterly report"}' | jq .

If server returns 429 with Retry-After header, the SDK should wait the indicated seconds (or compute a backoff schedule) before attempting another request.
